scope: Seventeen already inspected development photos; fixed perturbations of resized model RGB, no geometry/annotation/threshold changes. Padding remains unchanged. Appearance changes are empirical sRGB transforms, not a calibrated camera model. No training, held-out selection, crop replay or deployment.
interpretation: On these fixed small perturbations the expanded model has average phase-invariant material changes of 0.97% to 2.06% of known-body pixels, depending on variant. Averages conceal larger per-photo effects.
Increasing orange/yellow exposure by 5% changes 7.70% of known-body material predictions and lowers observed disagreement from 39.29% to 28.71%. It remains unsuitable for reconstruction.
Small appearance changes affect predictions without moving a single corner or cutting path. This isolates a neural appearance sensitivity, but does not attribute every failure to it.
Systematically absent motifs, foreground clutter and unlabelled fine boundaries remain. Appearance augmentation is a testable follow-up, not an established solution.
No per-image best-variant selection, retraining, crop or solver run, production source change, or model deployment.
